questions.question: Explain two different Christian views about the Eucharist.

points.text: 1) Catholics believe in transubstantiation — the bread and wine literally become the body and blood of Christ during the Mass, even though they still appear as bread and wine. This is based on Jesus' words "This is my body" at the Last Supper. 2) Baptists and many Protestants see the Eucharist as a memorial — the bread and wine are symbols that remind believers of Christ's sacrifice on the cross.

questions.question: Explain why baptism is important for Christians.

points.text: Baptism is important because: it follows Jesus' own baptism by John (Mark 1:9-11); Jesus commanded his disciples to baptise (Matthew 28:19); it symbolises the washing away of sin and new life in Christ; it initiates the person into the Christian community; and Catholics believe it removes original sin. Different denominations practise baptism differently but all see it as a key Christian rite.
